title: Zoom, reflow, and text resizing
learningObjectives: Explain zoom, reflow, and text resizing and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Responsive accessibility includes allowing text enlargement and page reflow without loss of content or functionality. Layouts should avoid fixed dimensions that clip text and should remain usable at narrow viewport widths and high zoom levels.
understand.whyItMatters: Users may enlarge text or zoom the page to read comfortably. Fixed-height containers and non-wrapping layouts can hide content or force two-dimensional scrolling.
understand.analogy: Reflow is allowing a page to rearrange its furniture when the room becomes smaller.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The layout uses a flexible width, readable measure, and wrapping text instead of a fixed page width.

practise.guidedTask: Test at 200% zoom and a narrow viewport. Check that controls and text remain available without horizontal scrolling for ordinary content.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.

questions.prompt: What is the goal of reflow at high zoom?
options: Keep content and functionality available in a narrow layout
questions.answer: Keep content and functionality available in a narrow layout
questions.explanation: Reflow adapts layout so users can access content without unnecessary two-dimensional scrolling.

options: Test actual browser behaviour and provide accessible fallbacks
Assume the browser always behaves exactly as expected
questions.answer: Test actual browser behaviour and provide accessible fallbacks
questions.explanation: Reliable web work combines standards knowledge with real testing and inclusive fallbacks.
